concern_details.detail: main components involved in registration and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: All seven lifelines appear in the code path (registration.html/app.js -> AuthenticationController.register -> LibraryFacade.register -> UserManager.register -> Student/LibrarianFactory, UserRegistry -> PersistenceManager). Each lifeline header now gives a one-line responsibility, and those match the code: UserManager validates, checks uniqueness, chooses the factory and persists (UserManager.java:65-97); LibraryFacade only forwards (LibraryFacade register is a one-line delegation); PersistenceManager.save runs the transaction with rollback (PersistenceManager.java:19-43). RestExceptionHandler is visible, merged into the controller lifeline as 'exception to status'.

concern_details.detail: how they interact when a new user creates an account
concern_details.why: Messages 01-12 follow the code order: format validation first (validate plus validateStudent/validateLibrarian, lines 67-75), then the email and identifier lookups (77-86), then the factory (89-90), registerUser/save (92) and the save-failure throw (93-94). The nested alts now put each guard after the step that decides it. The three outcomes a tester will see are all drawn: 200 UserDTO, 400 {error} for bad format or duplicate, and an unmapped RuntimeException when save returns false. One small gap: the [save ok] / [save returned false] guard depends on a boolean returned by PersistenceManager.save -> UserRegistry -> UserManager, and no return message is drawn. This is acceptable because the README says internal success replies were dropped on purpose.

concern_details.detail: main integration points to exercise in the tests
concern_details.why: IP1-IP4 are marked on the messages and explained in the legend. They match real seams in the code: the HTTP form parameters (form-urlencoded @RequestParam, with a Swing client that bypasses the step), validation plus the exception-to-HTTP mapping (RestExceptionHandler.java:19-22 maps only IllegalArgumentException/IllegalStateException), the role-based factory choice (UserManager.java:89), and the JPA lookups and save transaction against MySQL. A tester can turn each IP directly into test cases.

level_why: Seven lifelines and twelve messages fit 'balanced'. The cuts are sensible: two uniqueness lookups are collapsed into one message, per-field validation rules are a guard rather than self-messages, internal success replies are dropped, and the Swing client is a legend remark. Nothing should be added that would push the view past balanced. There is also nothing worth cutting: LibraryFacade forwards only, but it is the shared entry point for REST and Swing, so it is a real integration seam.
unsupported: Message 08 says 'Student -> StudentFactory, otherwise LibrarianFactory'. This matches UserManager.java:89. The legend wording 'unknown role rejected earlier' is also correct, because isValidRole at UserManager.java:54/169 accepts only Student or Librarian. No unsupported elements or relations were found.
'default 500' for the unmapped RuntimeException is inferred from Spring's default behaviour, not from code in the repository. It is plausible, and the README flags it as unverified.
missing: Minor: the duplicate check is really two different lookups. The email lookup runs against User (any role). The identifier lookup runs against Student.studentNumber or Librarian.internalIdentifierCode depending on role (UserRegistry.java:37-60). The collapsed message 05 could say 'email (any role) / identifier (per role) used?' so that the tester designs both duplicate cases for each role. This is a label change, not an extra message.
uml: Exception replies 04, 07 and 12 go from UserManager straight to the controller lifeline, but UserManager's caller is LibraryFacade. In UML a reply returns to the caller, so the arrows should end at the facade activation (or go facade -> controller). Here the 'via facade' label stands in for that. This is minor.

One lifeline stands for two classifiers ('AuthenticationController + RestExceptionHandler'). Strictly, a lifeline represents one participant. This is acceptable as a deliberate simplification at the balanced level, but it is not pure UML.
The 'IPn' prefixes in message labels are annotations, not UML notation. They are harmless because the legend explains them, and they are not stereotypes.
fixes: Optional: end the exception replies (04, 07, 12) at LibraryFacade, or label them as propagating through it, so that the reply targets the caller as UML requires.
Optional: relabel message 05 as 'email (any role) / identifier (per role) used?' so both duplicate cases are visible for each role.
